claim: Dynamin mediates membrane fission during endocytosis.
source: Dynamin, which mediates membrane fission during endocytosis, binds endophilin and other members of the Bin-Amphiphysin-Rvs (BAR) protein family.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as an established fact about dynamin's function.

claim: Dynamin binds endophilin and other members of the Bin-Amphiphysin-Rvs (BAR) protein family.
source: Dynamin, which mediates membrane fission during endocytosis, binds endophilin and other members of the Bin-Amphiphysin-Rvs (BAR) protein family.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as an established fact about dynamin-endophilin interactions.

claim: Dynamin-mediated membrane fission is potently inhibited in vitro when an excess of endophilin co-assembles with dynamin around membrane tubules.
source: Here, we show that dynamin-mediated membrane fission is potently inhibited in vitro when an excess of endophilin co-assembles with dynamin around membrane tubules.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: Endophilin intercalates between turns of the dynamin helix.
source: We further show by electron microscopy that endophilin intercalates between turns of the dynamin helix and impairs fission by preventing trans interactions between dynamin rungs that are thought to play critical roles in membrane constriction.
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Endophilin impairs fission by preventing trans interactions between dynamin rungs.
source: We further show by electron microscopy that endophilin intercalates between turns of the dynamin helix and impairs fission by preventing trans interactions between dynamin rungs that are thought to play critical roles in membrane constriction.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural observations in Figure 3 combined with the functional data in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: Trans interactions between dynamin rungs are thought to play critical roles in membrane constriction.
source: We further show by electron microscopy that endophilin intercalates between turns of the dynamin helix and impairs fission by preventing trans interactions between dynamin rungs that are thought to play critical roles in membrane constriction.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about dynamin mechanism.

claim: Overexpression of endophilin delayed both fission and transferrin uptake in living cells.
source: In living cells, overexpression of endophilin delayed both fission and transferrin uptake.
evidence: This is supported by the cell-based experiments shown in Figure 4.

claim: Endophilin helps shape endocytic tubules and recruit dynamin to endocytic sites.
source: Together, our observations suggest that while endophilin helps shape endocytic tubules and recruit dynamin to endocytic sites, it can also block membrane fission when present in excess by inhibiting inter-dynamin interactions.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge from prior literature.

claim: Endophilin can block membrane fission when present in excess by inhibiting inter-dynamin interactions.
source: Together, our observations suggest that while endophilin helps shape endocytic tubules and recruit dynamin to endocytic sites, it can also block membrane fission when present in excess by inhibiting inter-dynamin interactions.
evidence: This is the main conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The sequence of recruitment and the relative stoichiometry of endophilin and dynamin may be critical to regulated endocytic fission.
source: The sequence of recruitment and the relative stoichiometry of the two proteins may be critical to regulated endocytic fission.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion based on the experimental findings.

claim: Dynamin is a 97 kDa GTPase.
source: Dynamin is a 97 kDa GTPase that mediates membrane fission in several endocytic routes.
evidence: This is established knowledge about dynamin's molecular properties.

claim: Dynamin mediates membrane fission in several endocytic routes.
source: Dynamin is a 97 kDa GTPase that mediates membrane fission in several endocytic routes.
evidence: This is established knowledge about dynamin's function.

claim: Dynamin forms tetramers in solution via the stalk domain.
source: Dynamin forms tetramers in solution via the stalk domain (Muhlberg et al., 1997; Reubold et al., 2015) and polymers around membrane tubes (Sweitzer and Hinshaw, 1998; Takei et al., 1995).
evidence: This is supported by cited references.

claim: Dynamin forms polymers around membrane tubes.
source: Dynamin forms tetramers in solution via the stalk domain (Muhlberg et al., 1997; Reubold et al., 2015) and polymers around membrane tubes (Sweitzer and Hinshaw, 1998; Takei et al., 1995).
evidence: This is supported by cited references.

claim: Polymeric forms of dynamin have a GTPase activity increased up to a 1000-fold over basal hydrolysis rates.
source: Polymeric forms have a GTPase activity increased up to a 1000-fold over basal hydrolysis rates (Stowell et al., 1999).
evidence: This is supported by a cited reference.

claim: The increase in GTPase activity is proposed to result from trans interactions between GTPase (G) domains of adjacent turns of a dynamin helical polymer.
source: This increase is proposed to result from trans interactions between GTPase (G) domains of adjacent turns of a dynamin helical polymer (Chappie et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a mechanistic proposal supported by a cited reference.

claim: Constriction of the dynamin polymer is required for membrane fission.
source: Constriction of the dynamin polymer is required for membrane fission (Antonny et al., 2016), but how GTPase activity drives constriction is still debated.
evidence: This is supported by a cited reference.

claim: How GTPase activity drives constriction is still debated.
source: Constriction of the dynamin polymer is required for membrane fission (Antonny et al., 2016), but how GTPase activity drives constriction is still debated.
evidence: This acknowledges ongoing scientific debate in the field.

claim: The disassembly model proposes that dynamin assembles into a highly constricted helix in the GTP-loaded state and that GTP-hydrolysis-dependent disassembly is required for fission.
source: The disassembly model proposes that dynamin assembles into a highly constricted helix in the GTP-loaded state and that GTP-hydrolysis-dependent disassembly is required for fission (Shnyrova et al., 2013).
evidence: This describes a mechanistic model supported by a cited reference.

claim: In the constriction/ratchet model, dynamin G domains are proposed to act as motor heads that use GTP hydrolysis energy to drive relative displacement of helical turns and thereby decrease the diameter of the dynamin helix to constrict the underlying membrane tube.
source: In the constriction/ratchet model, dynamin G domains are proposed to act as motor heads that use GTP hydrolysis energy to drive relative displacement of helical turns and thereby decrease the diameter of the dynamin helix to constrict the underlying membrane tube.
evidence: This describes an alternative mechanistic model.

claim: Spontaneous fission takes place at the edge of the constricted tube due to thermal fluctuations according to the constriction/ratchet model.
source: Spontaneous fission then takes place at the edge of the constricted tube due to thermal fluctuations (Morlot et al., 2012).
evidence: This is part of the constriction/ratchet model supported by a cited reference.

claim: Dynamin is recruited to endocytic vesicle necks just before fission in the cell.
source: In the cell, dynamin is recruited to endocytic vesicle necks just before fission (Taylor et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a cited reference.

claim: Dynamin-binding N-BAR domain containing proteins are proposed to participate in dynamin recruitment.
source: The dynamin-binding N-BAR domain containing proteins are proposed to participate in this recruitment (Ferguson and De Camilli, 2012; Taylor et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by cited references.

claim: N-BAR domains are a subfamily of the crescent-shaped BIN-Amphiphysin-Rvs (BAR) domains with an additional N-terminal amphipathic helix.
source: N-BAR domains are a subfamily of the crescent-shaped BIN-Amphiphysin-Rvs (BAR) domains (Frost et al., 2009; Peter et al., 2004) with an additional N-terminal amphipathic helix.
evidence: This is a structural description supported by cited references.

claim: N-BAR proteins sense and induce membrane curvature.
source: N-BAR proteins sense and induce membrane curvature and are thus proposed to either help induce or bind avidly to the highly curved necks of endocytic pits (Farsad et al., 2001; Peter et al., 2004; Takei et al., 1999).
evidence: This is supported by cited references.

claim: N-BAR proteins are proposed to either help induce or bind avidly to the highly curved necks of endocytic pits.
source: N-BAR proteins sense and induce membrane curvature and are thus proposed to either help induce or bind avidly to the highly curved necks of endocytic pits (Farsad et al., 2001; Peter et al., 2004; Takei et al., 1999).
evidence: This is a functional proposal supported by cited references.

claim: The SH3 domain of N-BAR proteins binds to dynamin's proline-rich domain (PRD).
source: The SH3 domain of N-BAR proteins binds to dynamin's proline-rich domain (PRD) (Grabs et al., 1997; Ringstad et al., 1997) recruiting dynamin to vesicle necks (Sundborger et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by cited references.

claim: The SH3 domain of N-BAR proteins recruits dynamin to vesicle necks.
source: The SH3 domain of N-BAR proteins binds to dynamin's proline-rich domain (PRD) (Grabs et al., 1997; Ringstad et al., 1997) recruiting dynamin to vesicle necks (Sundborger et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a cited reference.

claim: N-BAR proteins have been proposed to directly participate in membrane fission, as their N-terminal alpha-helix induces membrane curvature.
source: N-BAR proteins have been proposed to directly participate in membrane fission, as their N-terminal alpha-helix induces membrane curvature, thus promoting constriction and possibly fission (Boucrot et al., 2012; Farsad et al., 2001).
evidence: This is a mechanistic proposal supported by cited references.

claim: The BAR domain is proposed to act as a stable scaffold, blocking further constriction below its preferred curvature and thereby stabilizing a tubule of a given diameter and inhibiting fission.
source: However, the role of N-BAR proteins in membrane fission is still unclear: the BAR domain is also proposed to act as a stable scaffold, blocking further constriction below its preferred curvature and thereby stabilizing a tubule of a given diameter and inhibiting fission (Boucrot et al., 2012).
evidence: This is an alternative mechanistic proposal supported by a cited reference.

claim: The BAR domain scaffold was proposed to hinder lipid diffusion, promoting fission of tubules under pulling forces.
source: This scaffold was also proposed to hinder lipid diffusion, promoting fission of tubules under pulling forces (Renard et al., 2015; Simunovic et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a mechanistic proposal supported by cited references.

claim: Amphiphysin was proposed to enhance dynamin-mediated membrane fission.
source: The contribution of N-BAR proteins to membrane fission mediated by dynamin is even less clear: amphiphysin was proposed to enhance dynamin-mediated membrane fission (Takei et al., 1999), a stimulatory effect later found to be curvature-dependent (Yoshida et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by a cited reference.

claim: The stimulatory effect of amphiphysin on dynamin-mediated membrane fission was later found to be curvature-dependent.
source: The contribution of N-BAR proteins to membrane fission mediated by dynamin is even less clear: amphiphysin was proposed to enhance dynamin-mediated membrane fission (Takei et al., 1999), a stimulatory effect later found to be curvature-dependent (Yoshida et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by a cited reference.

claim: Early findings showed that endophilin inhibited dynamin-mediated membrane fission.
source: Early findings showed that endophilin inhibited dynamin-mediated membrane fission (Farsad et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by a cited reference.

claim: Different results regarding endophilin's effect on dynamin-mediated fission were obtained in other assays.
source: However, different results were obtained in other assays (Meinecke et al., 2013; Neumann and Schmid, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by cited references.

claim: A fast endocytic pathway strictly depends on endophilinA2.
source: Moreover, a fast endocytic pathway strictly depends on endophilinA2, which may indicate that endophilin proteins can facilitate dynamin-mediated fission in certain contexts (Boucrot et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a cited reference.

claim: EndophilinA2 dependence may indicate that endophilin proteins can facilitate dynamin-mediated fission in certain contexts.
source: Moreover, a fast endocytic pathway strictly depends on endophilinA2, which may indicate that endophilin proteins can facilitate dynamin-mediated fission in certain contexts (Boucrot et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of cited findings.

claim: Tubules coated by dynamin alone underwent fission within a few seconds upon GTP addition.
source: Upon GTP addition (t = 0 s), the tubules coated by dynamin alone underwent fission within a few seconds as previously described (Roux et al., 2006), while tubules coated by endophilin and dynamin did not break nor alter their shape (see Figure 1A,B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A and cited reference.

claim: Tubules coated by endophilin and dynamin did not break nor alter their shape upon GTP addition.
source: Upon GTP addition (t = 0 s), the tubules coated by dynamin alone underwent fission within a few seconds as previously described (Roux et al., 2006), while tubules coated by endophilin and dynamin did not break nor alter their shape (see Figure 1A,B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: A fourfold excess of endophilin reduced the GTPase activity of liposome-bound dynamin by half.
source: We first performed a GTPase malachite green assay and found that a fourfold excess of endophilin reduced the GTPase activity of liposome-bound dynamin by half (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B), as previously published (Farsad et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B and a cited reference.

claim: Beads rotated with an average speed of 8–9 rotations/second with dynamin alone.
source: As previously shown, beads rotated with an average speed of 8–9 rotations/second with dynamin alone, whereas no rotation was observed in the presence of endophilin (Figure 1D,E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D,E.

claim: No rotation was observed in the presence of endophilin.
source: As previously shown, beads rotated with an average speed of 8–9 rotations/second with dynamin alone, whereas no rotation was observed in the presence of endophilin (Figure 1D,E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D,E.

claim: Endophilin blocked mechano-chemical constriction of dynamin and subsequent membrane fission.
source: These results showed that endophilin blocked mechano-chemical constriction of dynamin and subsequent membrane fission.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the bead rotation experiments.

claim: At low endophilin/dynamin ratios (0.5x/1x), fission was delayed.
source: At low endophilin/dynamin ratios (0.5x/1x), fission was delayed (39.5 ± 3.8 s for ratio 0.5x and 52.8 ± 7.8 s for ratio 1x, compared to 15.8 ± 3.7 s for dynamin alone; Figure 2E,F,G).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2E,F,G.

claim: At higher endophilin ratios (2x and 4x), membrane fission was dramatically inhibited or completely inhibited.
source: At higher endophilin ratios, where both dynamin and endophilin are bound to the tube (Figure 2D), membrane fission was dramatically inhibited (2x) or completely inhibited (4x) (Figure 2E,F,G).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D,E,F,G.

claim: No difference in fission efficiency of dynamin was observed for the SH3 domain alone at 4x endophilin-dynamin concentration ratio.
source: No difference in fission efficiency of dynamin was observed for the SH3 domain (Figure 2H,I).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2H,I.

claim: The N-BAR domain alone significantly decreased the fission rate.
source: By contrast, the N-BAR domain alone significantly decreased the fission rate (Figure 2H,J), while fission efficiency was reduced only slightly (Figure 2H,I).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2H,I,J.

claim: The N-BAR domain alone reduced fission efficiency only slightly.
source: By contrast, the N-BAR domain alone significantly decreased the fission rate (Figure 2H,J), while fission efficiency was reduced only slightly (Figure 2H,I).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2H,I.

claim: Trans G domain interactions have been proposed to be responsible for GTPase-dependent conformational changes and constriction.
source: These trans G domain interactions have been proposed to be responsible for GTPase-dependent conformational changes and constriction, thus precluding G domain interactings may inhibit fission (Chappie et al., 2010; Chappie et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by cited references.

claim: The dynamin signal was lower when endophilin was co-injected, as compared to dynamin alone.
source: The dynamin signal was lower when endophilin was co-injected, as compared to dynamin alone (Figure 2K,N), suggesting that endophilin was intercalating within the dynamin coat.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2K,N.

claim: Lower dynamin signal when endophilin was co-injected suggests that endophilin was intercalating within the dynamin coat.
source: The dynamin signal was lower when endophilin was co-injected, as compared to dynamin alone (Figure 2K,N), suggesting that endophilin was intercalating within the dynamin coat.
evidence: This is an inference from the fluorescence data.

claim: The endophilin signal on the tube increased with increasing endophilin concentration.
source: The endophilin signal on the tube increased, as expected, with increasing endophilin concentration (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The dynamin fluorescence reduced by 2–3 fold when endophilin was co-injected.
source: The dynamin fluorescence reduced by 2–3 fold (Figure 2K,O).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2K,O.

claim: Fission activity was dramatically reduced on tubes with the endophilin-dynamin co-complex.
source: Fission activity was dramatically reduced on tubes with the endophilin-dynamin co-complex, whereas it proceeded normally on tubes coated with dynamin only (Figure 2L).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2L.

claim: Fission proceeded normally on tubes coated with dynamin only.
source: Fission activity was dramatically reduced on tubes with the endophilin-dynamin co-complex, whereas it proceeded normally on tubes coated with dynamin only (Figure 2L).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2L.

claim: The molecular arrangement of the endophilin-dynamin co-complex was responsible for fission inhibition.
source: Our results thus support the idea that the molecular arrangement of the endophilin-dynamin co-complex was responsible for fission inhibition.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the fluorescence and fission data.

claim: The endophilin-dynamin co-complex suffered from highly variable spacing between turns of what appeared to be discrete dynamin oligomers (29.4 ± 5.2 nm).
source: In contrast with the endophilin-only and dynamin-only oligomers (Figure 3A–B), we observed that the endophilin-dynamin co-complex suffered from highly variable spacing between turns of what appeared to be discrete dynamin oligomers (29.4 ± 5.2 nm, Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by EM data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Endophilin-only coating has a ~5 nm spacing between turns.
source: Consistent with prior structural work, this approach resolved a uniform coating of endophilin-only with a ~5 nm spacing between turns (Figure 3A, [Mim et al., 2012]).
evidence: This is supported by EM data shown in Figure 3A and a cited reference.

claim: Averaging resolved the 'T-shaped' dynamin dimer, trans interactions between adjacent G-domains in the GMPPCP-bound state, and the phosphoinositide-binding pleckstrin homology (PH) domain.
source: Averaging resolved the 'T-shaped' dynamin dimer, trans interactions between adjacent G-domains in the GMPPCP-bound state, and the phosphoinositide-binding pleckstrin homology (PH) domain (Chappie et al., 2011; Zhang and Hinshaw, 2001) (Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by EM data shown in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1, and cited references.

claim: Analysis of the dynamin-only GMPPCP tubules revealed a mixture of 1-start (34%) and 2-start (66%) helices.
source: Further analysis of the dynamin-only GMPPCP tubules revealed a mixture of 1-start (34%) and 2-start (66%) helices (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by EM data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The stalk-to-stalk spacing between wild-type, full-length dynamin turns was nearly identical for the 1-start (13.9 nm) versus 2-start (14.0 nm) helices.
source: The stalk-to-stalk spacing between wild-type, full-length dynamin turns was nearly identical for the 1-start (13.9 nm) versus 2-start (14.0 nm) helices and is consistent with prior structural work using the dynamin truncations that lack the C-terminal proline-rich domain (Figure 3—figure supplement 1) (Antonny et al., 2016; Chappie et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by EM data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1 and cited references.

claim: Turns of a dynamin oligomer were spaced ~2 x further apart in the endophilin co-complex in either GDP or GMPPCP when compared with dynamin alone.
source: As previously reported (Farsad et al., 2001; Itoh et al., 2005; Sundborger et al., 2011; Takei et al., 1998; Takei et al., 1999), turns of a dynamin oligomer were spaced ~2 x further apart in the endophilin co-complex in either or GDP or GMPPCP when compared with dynamin alone when visualized with cryoEM or negative stain EM (Figure 3B–G).
evidence: This is supported by EM data shown in Figure 3B–G and cited references.

claim: CryoEM and 2D averaging revealed multiple endophilin molecules apparently interleaved between adjacent dynamin oligomers.
source: Consistently, cryoEM and 2D averaging revealed multiple endophilin molecules apparently interleaved between adjacent dynamin oligomers (Figure 3C), effectively separating the G domains.
evidence: This is supported by EM data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: When both endophilin and dynamin are bound to the membrane and to each other via SH3-PRD domain interactions, dynamin molecules from adjacent turns are too far apart to interact in trans.
source: In this arrangement, when both endophilin and dynamin are bound to the membrane and to each other via SH3-PRD domain interactions, dynamin molecules from adjacent turns are too far apart to interact in trans.
evidence: This is an inference from the structural data.

claim: Overexpression of endophilinA2-RFP in SKMEL-dynamin-GFP cells correlated with much brighter dynamin foci than in non-transfected cells.
source: Indeed, overexpression of endophilinA2-RFP in SKMEL-dynamin-GFP cells correlated with much brighter dynamin foci (Figure 4A, purple arrows) than in non-transfected cells (Figure 4A, green arrows).
evidence: This is supported by TIRFM data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: EndophilinA2-RFP colocalized with bright dynamin dots.
source: EndophilinA2-RFP colocalized with those bright dots.
evidence: This is supported by TIRFM data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Overexpression of endophilinA2-RFP delayed the kinetics of dynamin-GFP.
source: Overexpression of endophilinA2-RFP also delayed the kinetics of dynamin-GFP, as seen comparing kymographs taken in non-transfected cells (Figure 4B) with kymographs of cells overexpressing endophilinA2-RFP (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is supported by TIRFM data shown in Figure 4B,C.

claim: The average duration of dynamin2 foci was 13.3 ± 14.7 s in non-transfected cells.
source: The average duration of dynamin2 foci was 13.3 ± 14.7 s in non-transfected cells and went above 100 s when endophilinA2-RFP was overexpressed (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is supported by TIRFM data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: The average duration of dynamin2 foci went above 100 s when endophilinA2-RFP was overexpressed.
source: The average duration of dynamin2 foci was 13.3 ± 14.7 s in non-transfected cells and went above 100 s when endophilinA2-RFP was overexpressed (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is supported by TIRFM data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: SKMEL cells overexpressing endophilinA2-RFP show a lower internalization of transferrin.
source: Indeed, SKMEL cells overexpressing endophilinA2-RFP show a lower internalization of transferrin (Figure 4G).
evidence: This is supported by transferrin uptake data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: The transferrin uptake was significantly reduced in cells expressing endophilin above 10,000 F.A.U.
source: While the uptake of transferrin was not significantly different from the non-transfected cells when endophilin fluorescence was less than 10,000 F.A.U, the transferrin uptake was significantly reduced in cells expressing endophilin above 10,000 F.A.U (Figure 4H).
evidence: This is supported by transferrin uptake data shown in Figure 4H.

claim: Endophilin over-expression is inversely correlated to transferrin uptake in these cells.
source: Thus, endophilin over-expression is inversely correlated to transferrin uptake in these cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the transferrin uptake data.

claim: When dynamin2-cherry and endophilinA2-GFP were co-overexpressed in SKMEL dynamin2-GFP cells, no significant inhibition of the transferrin uptake was observed.
source: Indeed, when dynamin2-cherry and endophilinA2-GFP were co-overexpressed in SKMEL dynamin2-GFP cells, no significant inhibition of the transferrin uptake was observed (Figure 4H, Dyn2 OE).
evidence: This is supported by transferrin uptake data shown in Figure 4H.

claim: Co-assembly with endophilin can inhibit dynamin-mediated fission in a concentration-dependent manner in vivo.
source: From these in vivo results, we concluded that co-assembly with endophilin can inhibit dynamin-mediated fission in a concentration-dependent manner.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the cell-based experiments.

claim: The non-physiological 4x molar excess of endophilin inhibits fission completely by blocking dynamin constriction.
source: In this study, we have tested the effect of endophilin on dynamin's membrane fission activity. Our results show that the non-physiological 4x molar excess of endophilin inhibits fission completely by blocking dynamin constriction.
evidence: This is a summary of the main findings from the in vitro experiments.

claim: The inhibition was not only a time delay but also a decrease in fission efficiency up to a complete blockage.
source: We measured fission rates and efficiencies for different endophilin-dynamin molar ratios in a cell-free system and concluded that the inhibition was not only a time delay but also a decrease in fission efficiency up to a complete blockage.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the tube pulling experiments.

claim: Both endophilin's membrane binding N-BAR domain and direct dynamin binding SH3 domain contributed to full inhibition.
source: Deletion construct experiments indicated that both endophilin's membrane binding N-BAR domain and direct dynamin binding SH3 domain contributed to full inhibition.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the domain deletion experiments.

claim: Turns of endophilin intercalate between turns of dynamin polymers.
source: We have used negative stain EM and cryoEM to visualize the endophilin-dynamin membrane bound co-complex and found that turns of endophilin intercalate between turns of dynamin polymers (Figure 3, model in Figure 4J).
evidence: This is supported by EM data shown in Figure 3 and the model in Figure 4J.

claim: The structural arrangement of endophilin intercalating between dynamin turns explains the apparent increase in dynamin pitch reported earlier on blocked and elongated vesicle necks or tubular membranes.
source: This structural arrangement explains the apparent increase in dynamin pitch reported earlier on blocked and elongated vesicle necks or tubular membranes (Iversen et al., 2003; Takei et al., 1998; Takei et al., 1995).
evidence: This is an inference connecting the current structural findings to prior observations.

claim: All known BAR, N-BAR and F-BAR partners of dynamin were shown to change the architecture of the dynamin coat in similar ways when co-assembled on membrane tubules.
source: Interestingly, all known BAR, N-BAR and F-BAR partners of dynamin were shown to change the architecture of the dynamin coat in similar ways when co-assembled on membrane tubules (Itoh et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by a cited reference.

claim: Many BAR family proteins with dynamin-binding SH3 domains can potentially inhibit membrane fission by co-assembling with dynamin polymers when present in stoichiometric excess relative to dynamin.
source: This observation and our results suggest that many BAR family proteins with dynamin-binding SH3 domains can potentially inhibit membrane fission by co-assembling with dynamin polymers when present in stoichiometric excess relative to dynamin.
evidence: This is a speculative generalization based on the current findings and prior observations.

claim: The N-terminal amphipathic helices of endophilins have been shown to promote fission by inducing very high curvature.
source: While the N-terminal amphipathic helices have been shown to promote fission by inducing very high curvature, the crescent shape of the BAR domain counteracted this effect by fixing membrane curvature above the spontaneous fission threshold (Boucrot et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a cited reference.

claim: The crescent shape of the BAR domain counteracted the fission-promoting effect by fixing membrane curvature above the spontaneous fission threshold.
source: While the N-terminal amphipathic helices have been shown to promote fission by inducing very high curvature, the crescent shape of the BAR domain counteracted this effect by fixing membrane curvature above the spontaneous fission threshold (Boucrot et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a cited reference.

claim: EndophilinA2 was recently shown to be needed for fission in clathrin-independent endocytic pathways specific to G-coupled receptors.
source: But endophilinA2 was recently shown to be needed for fission in clathrin-independent endocytic pathways specific to G-coupled receptors (Boucrot et al., 2015), or to Shiga-toxin (Renard et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by cited references.

claim: EndophilinA2 was recently shown to be needed for fission in clathrin-independent endocytic pathways specific to Shiga-toxin.
source: But endophilinA2 was recently shown to be needed for fission in clathrin-independent endocytic pathways specific to G-coupled receptors (Boucrot et al., 2015), or to Shiga-toxin (Renard et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a cited reference.

claim: EndophilinA2 polymerizes into rigid scaffolds around preformed membrane tubules.
source: EndophilinA2 polymerizes into rigid scaffolds around preformed membrane tubules (Simunovic et al., 2016), which block diffusion of lipids when the membrane tube is under tension, driving thinning and fission of the tube (Renard et al., 2015; Simunovic et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by cited references.

claim: EndophilinA2 scaffolds block diffusion of lipids when the membrane tube is under tension, driving thinning and fission of the tube.
source: EndophilinA2 polymerizes into rigid scaffolds around preformed membrane tubules (Simunovic et al., 2016), which block diffusion of lipids when the membrane tube is under tension, driving thinning and fission of the tube (Renard et al., 2015; Simunovic et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by cited references.

claim: Overexpression of endophilin A2 inhibits fission at clathrin-coated pits, where dynamin is the primary fission machinery.
source: In contrast, we show here that overexpression of endophilin A2 inhibits fission at clathrin-coated pits, where dynamin is the primary fission machinery (Figure 4), which is consistent with the inhibitory action of endophilin on dynamin-dependent fission in our in vitro studies.
evidence: This is supported by the cell-based experiments shown in Figure 4.

claim: Endophilin participates in the recruitment of dynamin to vesicle necks pointing to a positive role in promoting fission.
source: Endophilin participates in the recruitment of dynamin to vesicle necks pointing to a positive role in promoting fission (Farsad et al., 2001; Gad et al., 2000; Shupliakov et al., 1997; Sundborger et al., 2011; Wigge et al., 1997).
evidence: This is supported by cited references.
